subject: Running into trouble with an 'R' Notebook

messages.author: 3f14800488510fbc
messages.subject: Running into trouble with an 'R' Notebook
parts:
Hello Davis R users,

I would have come by in person today, however, the 'R' class I'm in is scheduled at the same time are the meetup.

So, I seem to have run into a mysterious problem installing the "stringr" package that no one else in my 'R' class had, and the teacher was rather puzzled. 

I came and visited Michelle in the code lab, and she also wasn't sure what's going on, and figured I ought to see if any of you might know what's going on before I bug the professor with it again.   

I've done a lot of basic trouble shooting: uninstalling and reinstalling 'R', verifying nothing was wrong with the notebook with its author, etc.  Michael and I also tried doing everything suggested on the Stack Overflow page on this issue, and that didn't work either. 

So wow, yes, myself and a couple others are now quite stumped. 

The basics of the issue are below. Any and all help in approaching this mystery would be wonderful. Thank you so much. ~H


The deets:


I’m working on a Mac with MacOS Mojave v10.14.6

 

I’m running the install line:

 

install.packages("stringr")

library(stringr)

 

But then it doesn't work and rather I get the error message:

 

> install.packages("stringr")

also installing the dependency ‘stringi’

 

 

  There is a binary version available but the source version is later:

        binary source needs_compilation

stringi  1.4.3  1.4.4              TRUE

 

Do you want to install from sources the package which needs compilation? (Yes/no/cancel) library(stringr)

Error in install.packages : Unrecognized response “library(stringr)”

>

messages.author: 4b16035cff9b0f8a
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Running into trouble with an 'R' Notebook
parts:
What version of R? What version of stringr is it attempting to install? The error implies that the compilation of stringi is failing and then stringr can't load, which makes sense because stringr is just a wrapper for the stringi functions. Some quick digging indicates that there is no compiled version of 1.44 yet although the source code is 1.44. Are you choosing yes to the compile? 

Obviously this is something that would be better handled with actual access to the computer. I can help you troubleshoot more if nobody else points out a known bug and you want to contact me privately.


Thanks,
Erica

--
Erica Rettig
Ph.D. Candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology, UC Davis

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Running into trouble with an 'R' Notebook
parts:
What does it do if you try and install stringi on its own?

If you are compiling, have you made sure your compilation tools are setup?

xcode-select --install

Are these already installed or does it ask you to install them?

If a package requires fortran you might need the tools from here:
https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/tools/

This page also has the "right" version of clang on it. You could see if that is a problem as well, but those errors will look different.

B

messages.author: 200f38cfd2bed040
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Running into trouble with an 'R' Notebook
parts:
So I'm no expert, and maybe this is a typo instead of your actual problem, but the problem with the code in your message is that you're running two lines of code - the first line asks for a response and then the second line is auto-filled in that response blank, which because it's a library command, isn't a valid response for the response requested by the first line. If your message does represent your problem accurately, it should be fixed by running the first line (install.packages('stringr')), typing in one of the required responses (probably "Yes"), and then running the second line.

Sorry if that's not actually your problem and this isn't helpful!
